chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Muhammad Al-Farra, who said:

I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Follow one with the other (Hajj and Umrah), for they eliminate poverty and sins, just as the bellows eliminates the dross of iron.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of performing Hajj and Umrah together according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the virtue of linking Hajj and Umrah (Qiran or Tamattu') as a means of comprehensive purification. The metaphor of the 'kir' (blacksmith's bellows) underscores the transformative power of these rituals, suggesting that just as fire removes dross from iron, the spiritual intensity of these pilgrimages eradicates both material scarcity and spiritual impurities. This aligns with Shia scholarly emphasis on the holistic benefit of worship, addressing both the soul and worldly conditions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Muhammad Al Farra who said,

‘I heard Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Pursue between the Hajj and the Umra, for these two negate the poverty and the sins, just as the bellows negate the slag of the iron’.
en.sarwar: 12. Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Muhammad al-Farra’ who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Perform al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah consecutively; they remove poverty and sins just as al-Kir (a bellowing kiln) removes impurities from iron.’””
